{{nihongo|'''Wanishita Shrine (Ichinomoto)'''|和爾下神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

'''Wanishita Shrine''' (わにしたじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Ichinomoto|ja|櫟本町|ko|이치노모토정|qid=Q17174137}}, {{ill|Tenri, Nara|Q502196|qid=Q502196}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|Q131287|qid=Q131287}}. It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, formerly a {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, and a {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}{{sfn|Nara Prefectural History|p=72}}.

=== History ===
The shrine stands where the old Tatsuta Road and {{ill|Kami Kaidō|ja|上街道 (上ツ道)|qid=Q11360095|lt=Kami-tsu-michi}} intersect{{sfn|Nara Prefectural History|p=329}}{{sfn|Great Dictionary of Temples and Shrines|p=832}}. Tenno{{sfn|Great Dictionary of Temples and Shrines|p=832}}. It is considered one of the "two seats of Wanishita Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} for Soekami District{{sfn|Great Dictionary of Temples and Shrines|p=832}}. Originally, this shrine appears to have enshrined the ancestral deity of the Kakinomoto clan, relatives of the {{ill|Wani clan|Q11417873|qid=Q11417873}}, and that original deity may have been the Wani ancestor {{ill|Prince Ametarashihiko|ja|天足彦国押人命|qid=Q11443593}}{{sfn|Nara Prefectural History|p=329}}.

The shrine site was in Ichii-no-sho, an estate of {{ill|Tōdai-ji|Q460367|qid=Q460367}}. ''{{ill|Tōdaiji Zoku Yōroku|ja|東大寺続要録|qid=Q11526471}}'' records that from the Jingo-keiun era, irrigation ponds and waterways were developed and Yokota Road (Tatsuta Road) was repaired{{sfn|Nara Prefectural History|p=329}}{{sfn|Great Dictionary of Temples and Shrines|p=832}}. ''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kakinomoto Ason Hitomaro Kanmon}}'' says, "Beside Isonokami Temple in Soekami District there is a shrine called Harumichi-sha, and within it a temple called Kakinomoto-dera," indicating the old use of the name Harumichi and the existence of Kakinomoto-dera as the shrine-temple{{sfn|Nara Prefectural History|p=329}}{{sfn|Great Dictionary of Temples and Shrines|p=832}}. Nara-period roof tiles were excavated from Hitomaru-zuka in the former precincts of Kakinomoto-dera{{sfn|Nara Prefectural History|p=329}}{{sfn|Great Dictionary of Temples and Shrines|p=832}}.

=== Precincts ===
At the western foot of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mount Todai-ji}}, the precinct corresponds to the rear circular section of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Wanishita Shrine Kofun}}, part of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Todai-ji-yama Kofun group}}{{sfn|Great Dictionary of Temples and Shrines|p=832}}.

=== Cultural properties ===
=== Important Cultural Property ===
* Main hall
A three-bay {{ill|Kirizuma-style|Q13308575|qid=Q13308575}} structure with cypress bark roof, built in the {{ill|Azuchi–Momoyama period|Q319531|qid=Q319531|lt=Momoyama period}}. National Important Cultural Property.<ref>[http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kurashi/kyouiku/bunkazai/1391410354160.html Wanishita Shrine (Tenri City site)]</ref>
